chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Safwan ibn al-Hakm al-Hannat, who said: Zayd al-Shahham narrated to me, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him),

He said: The enjoyment (ni'mah) in this world is security (al-amn), and health of the body; and the complete enjoyment in the Hereafter is entering Paradise. And no servant ever attains complete enjoyment unless he enters Paradise.

key_terms.الْآخِرَةِ: The Hereafter, the life to come

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of true enjoyment (ni'mah) in this world and the hereafter according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration in *Mani al-Akhbar* to distinguish between transient worldly comforts and eternal spiritual fulfillment, a key theme in Shia ethics regarding the hierarchy of blessings. The hadith posits that while security and health are genuine forms of *ni'mah*, they are incomplete without the ultimate reward of Paradise, thereby linking physical well-being to eschatological success. This perspective encourages believers to view worldly blessings as means to an end rather than ends in themselves, aligning with the Shia emphasis on *tawhid* in appreciation of divine favors.

en.basel-kadem: 86.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammed, from his father, from Hammad, from Huraiz, from Zurara, that he said: I asked Abu Ja’far, peace be upon him: Was the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, asked about children? He said: He was certainly asked, and he said: Allah is more knowledgeable of what they are to do. He then said: O Zurara, do you know what is (the meaning of) his saying: «Allah is more knowledgeable of what they are to do»? He said: No. He said: To Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, is the will with regards to them. Indeed, when the Day of Resurrection will be, to Him will children be brought, and so will an old man who had reached an old age and does not rationalize due to aging and senility, and the one who dies in a period in which there are two Prophets, and the insane and the fool who does not rationalize. All of them will argue against Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, to which Allah, Exalted is He, will send to them an Angel from the Angels who will stir up a fire and say: Indeed, your Lord is commanding you to stay firm in it. Then, those who stay in it, it will be cold and a cause of peace to him, and those who disobey him will be dragged to the Fire.
